extracted.intended_audience: science communicators / press officers and researchers in science journalism
extracted.subtask_short: writing press releases for scientific research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing press releases about scientific research aimed at newspaper coverage; emphasizes how journalists select and transform releases into news items. Draws on content analysis and interviews with Dutch news editors and science journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple language / minimal jargon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain English; avoid technical vocabulary that requires translation. Journalists prefer releases that are already in lay terms because time pressure discourages rewriting. Provide brief definitions or analogies rather than specialist terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear 'so what' / compelling story angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear "so what" framing; story angle, not just facts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the significance or human-interest angle. Frame findings in terms of relevance and implications so journalists can quickly see the news hook rather than having to infer it from raw results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local / practical relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect the research to local audiences or practical applications. Explicitly state geographic or societal connections that make the story relevant to a newspaper's readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizable source / institutional prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizable institution; sources matter (recognized journals, prestigious institutions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominently identify reputable institutions and high-profile journals. Journalists give more weight to releases from established organizations and well-known publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotable, accessible scientist quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief, pithy quotes from researchers that are easy to drop into an article. Avoid dense or highly technical quotes; provide one or two lines that convey significance in plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay summary before technical detail / pre-translated concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay summary precedes technical detail; pre-translated technical concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load a concise lay summary or key finding before presenting methods or caveats. Provide pre-digested explanations of technical concepts so journalists do not have to reinterpret them under time pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid complex methodological and statistical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on scientific research means avoidance of complex information; statistical caveats and methodological detail often get dropped
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect detailed methods, statistical caveats, sample-size discussions, limitations, or COI statements to survive into news copy. If such details are essential, offer a brief plain-language version and point to a link for full technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize news value over scientific significance
rubrics_metrics.description: News value ranks higher than scientific significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight aspects that make the story newsworthy (novelty, timeliness, conflict, human interest, practical impact) since journalists select stories based on perceived news value rather than purely scientific importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of translation to lay language
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease of translation to lay language matters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure sentences and paragraphs so they can be excerpted or paraphrased easily. Use clear leads, short paragraphs, and signpost language; provide plain-language summaries and analogies to facilitate quick rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide press-ready material (because journalists rely heavily on releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heavy reliance on press releases as source
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ready-to-use elements (headline suggestions, succinct lede, key facts, high-quality images, contact details). Because journalists often use releases as primary source material, making content plug-and-play increases the likelihood of coverage.
